name: LSM6DSLTR
title: iNEMO 6-axis inertial module: 3D accelerometer and 3D gyroscope
summary: A 6-axis inertial module combining a 3-axis accelerometer (±2/±4/±8/±16 g) and a 3-axis gyroscope (±125 to ±2000 dps) with a temperature sensor in a 2.5 x 3 x 0.83 mm 14-lead LGA. Both run together on 0.65 mA in high-performance mode, 0.45 mA in normal mode and 0.29 mA in low-power mode, from a 1.71 V to 3.6 V core supply and a separate 1.62 V to 3.6 V I/O supply. It talks I2C or SPI, buffers up to 4 kbytes in a FIFO and detects free-fall, wake-up, 6D orientation, taps, steps, tilt, wrist tilt and significant motion in hardware. A second I2C port can read up to four external sensors.
key_figures: 1.6 Hz (accelerometer low power) or 12.5 Hz to 6.66 kHz
0.65 mA typ high-performance (1.6 kHz), 0.45 mA normal (208 Hz), 0.29 mA low-power (52 Hz); 3 μA power-down
gyroscope 4 mdps/√Hz; accelerometer 90 μg/√Hz (±2 g) in high-performance mode
Vdd 1.71 V to 3.6 V; Vdd_IO 1.62 V to 3.6 V
I2C up to 400 kHz, SPI 3/4-wire up to 10 MHz; I2C master for external sensors

operation.text: A system-in-package with a 3-axis MEMS accelerometer and a 3-axis MEMS gyroscope, a CMOS interface chip trimmed to the sensing elements, an on-chip temperature sensor, a 4 kbyte FIFO and hardware blocks for motion events, pedometer, tilt, significant motion and timestamping. It can also act as a hub, reading up to four external sensors over its own I2C master and correcting an external magnetometer for hard and soft iron.

The pin 1 view marks linear axes X, Y and Z and the rotations about them: pitch (ΩP) about X, roll (ΩR) about Y, yaw (ΩY) about Z. The gyroscope output goes positive for counterclockwise rotation about an axis.

Mode 1: the host talks to the part over I2C or 3/4-wire SPI and SDx/SCx are tied to VDDIO or GND. Mode 2: the same host interface, plus an I2C master on SDx/SCx (MSDA/MSCL) for external sensors, with INT2 able to serve as the master's sync input MDRDY.

Accelerometer and gyroscope switch on and off on their own, each with its own ODR and power mode: accelerometer only, gyroscope only, or both. Writing ODR_XL[3:0] in CTRL1_XL (10h) wakes the accelerometer from power-down; ODR_G[3:0] in CTRL2_G (11h) wakes the gyroscope.

Power-down, low-power, normal and high-performance. With G_HM_MODE = 0 in CTRL7_G (16h) every ODR from 12.5 Hz to 6.66 kHz runs in high-performance mode. With G_HM_MODE = 1, 12.5, 26 and 52 Hz run in low-power mode and 104 and 208 Hz in normal mode.

Power-down, low-power, normal and high-performance. With XL_HM_MODE = 0 in CTRL6_C (15h) every ODR from 12.5 Hz to 6.66 kHz is high-performance. With XL_HM_MODE = 1, 1.6, 12.5, 26 and 52 Hz run in low-power mode and 104 and 208 Hz in normal mode.

ADC, an optional high-pass filter (HP_EN_G, cutoff by HPM_G), an optional low-pass LPF1 (LPF1_SEL_G, bandwidth by FTYPE[1:0]) and a final low-pass set by ODR_G, then the output registers and the FIFO. Mode 1 and Mode 2 use the same chain.

An analog anti-aliasing low-pass, the ADC, a digital LPF1 (LPF1_BW_SEL in CTRL1_XL) and a composite filter whose input is chosen by INPUT_COMPOSITE in CTRL8_XL: ODR/2 or ODR/4 low-passed data. The composite stage offers LPF2, a slope filter and a high-pass filter; the slope or high-pass output feeds wake-up and activity/inactivity (SLOPE_FDS), LPF2 can feed 6D/4D (LOW_PASS_ON_6D), and free-fall and the embedded functions take their own taps. With HP_REF_MODE on, the first output sample is not valid and must be thrown away.

4 kbytes, up to 4096 16-bit words, holding gyroscope, accelerometer, external sensor, step counter with timestamp, and temperature data. Writes are paced by the accelerometer/gyroscope data-ready (FIFO ODR no higher than either sensor's ODR), by the sensor hub data-ready, or by each detected step. Each data set can be decimated by 2, 3, 4, 8, 16 or 32 (FIFO_CTRL3, FIFO_CTRL4). The threshold FTH[10:0] sits in FIFO_CTRL1/2. FIFO_STATUS1 to 4 give overrun, full, empty, threshold and the count of unread words; INT1_CTRL and INT2_CTRL route these to the pins. Discard the first sample after switching into or out of FIFO mode.

Bypass (000): FIFO off and empty; also used to clear it. FIFO (001): fills until full, then stops; with STOP_ON_FTH = 1 the depth is cut to FTH. Continuous (110): newest data replaces oldest; OVER_RUN flags an overwrite, FTH flags reaching the threshold and a full flag can raise an interrupt. Continuous-to-FIFO (011): continuous while the chosen trigger bit (in FUNC_SRC1, TAP_SRC, WAKE_UP_SRC or D6D_SRC) is 0, FIFO mode once it is 1. Bypass-to-Continuous (100): held empty until the trigger is 1, then continuous.

Samples are stored as up to four 6-byte data sets: gyroscope first, accelerometer second, SENSORHUB1 to 6 third, and fourth either SENSORHUB7 to 12, step counter with timestamp, or temperature. Data are read 16 bits at a time from FIFO_DATA_OUT_L/H (3Eh/3Fh); FIFO_STATUS3/4 give the position in the repeating pattern of the next word. Set BDU for a clean read of the status and data registers.

Hardware tilt detection on the accelerometer alone signals whenever the device changes its tilt, with a programmable averaging window and threshold. In a trouser pocket it fires on sitting down or standing up and stays quiet while walking, running or climbing stairs.

Fires when the angle between a chosen accelerometer semi-axis (positive X by default) and the horizontal stays above a threshold for at least a latency time. It runs at 26 Hz from the accelerometer, so the accelerometer ODR must be 26 Hz or more. Enable with FUNC_EN and WRIST_TILT_EN in CTRL10_C (19h); route to INT2 with INT2_WRIST_TILT in DRDY_PULSE_CFG_G (0Bh); read WRIST_TILT_IA in FUNC_SRC2 (54h), which also clears a latched interrupt; WRIST_TILT_IA (55h) names the triggering axis. Threshold, latency and axis mask sit in bank B.

Free-fall, wake-up, 6D/4D orientation, single and double tap, and activity/inactivity are detected in hardware and enabled together by INTERRUPTS_ENABLE in TAP_CFG (58h). MD1_CFG (5Eh) and MD2_CFG (5Fh) route each event to INT1 or INT2; INT1_CTRL and INT2_CTRL route data-ready, FIFO and pedometer events. Each pin outputs the OR of the signals routed to it; INT2_on_INT1 puts everything on INT1. LIR in TAP_CFG latches the interrupt requests. Interrupt pins are push-pull or open-drain (PP_OD) and active high or low (H_LACTIVE).

Step detector and step counter run in hardware once FUNC_EN and PEDO_EN are set; the count sits in STEP_COUNTER_L/H (4Bh/4Ch) and overflow is flagged at 2^16. The minimum peak threshold, 2 g or 4 g processing (PEDO_FS), debounce steps and debounce time sit in bank A. Significant motion uses SM_THS (default 6). The timestamp of the last step is copied to STEP_TIMESTAMP_L/H.
TIMER_EN in CTRL10_C starts a 24-bit counter in TIMESTAMP0 to 2 (40h to 42h), with 1 LSB of 6.4 ms or 25 μs set by TIMER_HR. Writing AAh to TIMESTAMP2_REG resets it.

In Mode 2 the I2C master (MASTER_ON, needs FUNC_EN) reads up to four external sensors, set up through bank A: a 7-bit address and read/write bit, a register sub-address, a read count and a decimation for each. Results land in SENSORHUB1 to 18 (2Eh to 39h, 4Dh to 52h). The master is triggered by the accelerometer/gyroscope data-ready or by an external signal on INT2 (START_CONFIG). Pass-through mode connects the host bus to the external sensors. Hard-iron (IRON_EN) and soft-iron (SOFT_EN) correction can be applied to an external magnetometer, whose raw data appear in 66h to 6Bh.

INT2 can serve as a DEN input that stamps the LSB of selected gyroscope or accelerometer axes (DEN_X/Y/Z, DEN_XL_G in CTRL9_XL). Edge, level, latched-level or FIFO-enable triggering is chosen in CTRL6_C; DEN_LH sets its active level.

Each axis is a 16-bit two's-complement word in an L/H register pair; BLE swaps the byte order and BDU holds an output pair until both bytes are read. IF_INC (on by default) advances the address during multi-byte reads; the ROUNDING bits make burst reads wrap round a chosen set of output registers. STATUS_REG (1Eh) flags new temperature, gyroscope and accelerometer data. WHO_AM_I (0Fh) reads 6Ah.
X_OFS_USR and Y_OFS_USR are added to and Z_OFS_USR subtracted from the measured acceleration on their axes; each is two's complement from -127 to 127, weighted 2^-10 g or 2^-6 g by USR_OFF_W.
SW_RESET in CTRL3_C resets the device and clears itself; BOOT reloads the trimming values from memory. Turn-on time is 35 ms typ.

Slave in standard (100 kHz) and fast (400 kHz) mode, chosen by pulling CS high. SCL and SDA need external pull-ups to Vdd_IO. The address is 110101xb with x set by SDO/SA0, so two parts can share a bus. After the address byte comes an 8-bit register sub-address; reads use a repeated start. Writing I2C_disable = 1 in CTRL4_C leaves SPI only.

Slave, 4-wire (CS, SPC, SDI, SDO) by default or 3-wire with SIM = 1 in CTRL3_C, up to 10 MHz. CS goes low for a transfer; SPC idles high. Data change on the falling edge of SPC and are sampled on the rising edge. A transfer is 16 clocks: bit 0 is R/W (1 = read), bits 1 to 7 the register address, bits 8 to 15 the data, MSb first; each extra byte adds 8 clocks.
The core runs from Vdd and the I/O from Vdd_IO. Each takes a 100 nF ceramic capacitor placed as close to its pin as possible.

Bank A (sensor hub, pedometer, significant motion, magnetometer correction) opens with FUNC_CFG_EN = 1 in FUNC_CFG_ACCESS (01h); bank B (wrist tilt) when both FUNC_CFG_EN_B and FUNC_CFG_EN are 1. Change them only in power-down.
The LGA is ECOPACK, RoHS and Green compliant and qualified for soldering heat to JEDEC J-STD-020.

Zero-g and zero-rate levels come partly from mechanical stress on the MEMS, so they can shift a little after soldering to a board or other heavy stress. At rest on a level surface X and Y read 0 g and Z reads 1 g.
